Subject: Observability add-ons: pricing scenarios for Helio Health

Hi Rajiv —

Thanks again for the time yesterday. As discussed, I wanted to share two clear pricing scenarios so your procurement team can see trade-offs between retention, tracing volume, and the advanced dashboard seat model. The goal is to help Helio pick the path that meets clinical auditing needs without surprising egress/overage exposure.

Quick summary:
- Option A (Default): 30-day retention for traces + standard dashboards (seat-based). Predictable monthly fee + per-GB cold archive.
- Option B (Extended): 90-day retention, sampling on high-cardinality traces, advanced dashboards included (flat add-on with tiered seats). Higher base, lower overage risk.
- Option C (Elastic): 30-day active retention + on-demand archive retrievals billed at retrieval rate; discounted tracing ingestion with committed monthly volume.

Can you confirm which internal stakeholders should see a simple TCO comparison? If procurement prefers, we can convert Option B into a fixed commitment with a one-time onboarding credit to offset migration effort.

I've attached the latest ratecard and a short matrix that maps Helio's sizing estimates to each option (redwood-obs-ratecard-v3.pdf; helio-map-pricing-matrix.xlsx).

Next steps I propose:
1) You pick 1–2 preferred options for a short commercial sketch.
2) If procurement needs, we loop in Ben for discount rationale and Kimberly for SLA/retention exceptions.
3) We'll deliver a one-page mutual action plan and an estimated invoice impact.

Appreciate the signal on timing — want to get you a ready-to-sign path this week if possible.

Best,
Jordan Blake

Rajiv / Jordan —

Thanks for flagging the two asks. Quick answers and rationale below.

1) Archived traces and queryability (Option B):
- We offer a warm-archive tier where traces are retained for 90 days and can be queried without a retrieval fee, subject to an API rate cap (suitable for quarterly audits).
- For deep historical search beyond 90 days, there is an on-demand retrieval model. We can add a quarterly audit allowance (e.g., 5k queries / quarter) into the commitment to cover expected audit windows.

2) Dashboards licensing:
- We differentiate Edit seats vs View-only. Option B's "advanced dashboard bundle" is structured as: unlimited viewers + 10 editor seats per 100k MAUs equivalent; additional editors are prorated monthly.

Commercial concession idea: if Helio signs a 12-month commit on Option B at the committed tracing ingestion tier (we'd define the ingestion band in the matrix), we can:
- Waive the onboarding surcharge (one-time)
- Provide a 15% discount on the dashboard add-on for the first 6 months
- Include the quarterly audit allowance in the SOW

If that sounds like a direction, Jordan, let's draft a short amendment and a line-item sketch to share with Rajiv's procurement team.

Thanks,
Ben Carter
Senior Sales Manager | Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.com

Rajiv —

Appreciate the questions. Confirming Ben's notes and adding an operational clarity piece so procurement can finalize language:

Operational commitments we will include if Helio signs the 12-month Option B commit:
- SLA: 99.9% availability for dashboard queries; 99.5% for trace ingestion pipeline.
- Retention guarantees: 90-day warm retention with immutable audit snapshots retained for an additional 180 days in cold storage (read-only, retrieval fees waived for scheduled audit windows).
- Data access: role-based viewer/edit controls; unlimited viewer tokens, editor tokens billable as Ben described.
- Security: SOC 2 Type II attestation for the retention systems (we will provide the cert during contracting).

Commercial: Jordan / Ben — please confirm the following final sketch so procurement can include in our SOW:
- Base: Option B with 90-day retention (monthly base fee)
- Add-on: advanced dashboards (unlimited viewers + 10 editors)
- Concession: waive onboarding fee + 15% discount on dashboards for months 1–6 + quarterly audit allowance (up to 5k queries)

I'll prepare a redlineable SOW and attach the updated ratecard that reflects the concession. Rajiv — once you confirm the commercial sketch and we have the signatory details, we can route a DocuSign SOW.

Best,
